name: IN-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+21 partisan lean anchors the race firmly in Democratic territory
André Carson's incumbency and financial edge ($1.1M raised, $558K on hand) against a Republican challenger with no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic victory at 97-99%

model.rationale: The district's D+21 lean, Carson's incumbency, and his large fundraising advantage over an unfunded Republican challenger all point to an easy Democratic hold, and prediction markets agree at 97-99%. With no polling or spending signals suggesting competition, the forecast stays at a Safe D rating with a margin near the district's fundamental lean.
model.watch: Any late surge in Republican fundraising or outside spending, or unexpected polling showing a single-digit race, would be the first sign this seat is in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indianapolis-area IN-07 is one of the most Democratic-leaning districts in Indiana, with a partisan lean of D+21. André Carson, a long-serving incumbent, is running for another term and holds a substantial financial advantage, having raised over $1.1 million with $558,000 on hand. His Republican challenger, Patrick McAuley, shows no reported fundraising, and a Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, but prediction markets price a Democratic win at 97-99%. The combination of the district's strong lean, Carson's incumbency, and the absence of any competitive signals supports a Safe D forecast with an expected margin of roughly 25 points. The main uncertainty is the lack of polling, which widens uncertainty modestly but does not change the expected outcome.
